THE DELETION RESTRICTION METHOD FOR PLANE CURVE
GERM COMPLEMENT
YONGQIANG LIU
Abstract. We study the cohomology jump loci of rank one local systems for the plane
curve germ complement by the deletion restriction method. In particular, the deletion
restriction type results in this case only depend on the linking numbers between the
irreducible components of the plane curve germ.
1. Introduction
Let f : (C2, 0) →(C, 0) be a reduced plane curve singularity at the origin of C2. Let
f = Qr
i=1 fi be a decomposition of the germ f into irreducible factors fi in the factorial
ring O2 of analytic function germs. The assumption f being reduced means that all the
factors fi above are distinct.
In this paper, we always assume that r ≥2. Let B denote the small enough open ball
centred at the origin of C2. Set
Ci = {fi = 0} ∩B, U = B −Sr
i=1 Ci and U′ = B −Sr

Let j : U →U′ be the corresponding inclusion map, which induces a natural map on
the fundamental group level:
π1(U) →π1(U′).
What can we say about this natural map? In this paper, we answer the question on
the cohomology jump loci level. Since the homotopy type of the local complement are
determined by Puiseux pairs and linking numbers (see [Dim04, Theorem 2.2.11]), hence
so is this natural map. It turns out that our answer on the cohomology jump loci level
only depends on the linking numbers between C1 and Ci for all 1 < i ≤r.
First let us recall the deﬁnition of cohomology jump loci. Let Char(U) be the mod-
uli space of rank one C-local systems on U. Then Char(U) ∼= Hom(H1(U, Z), C∗) as
algebraic group. Notice that H1(U, Z) has a natural basis [γi]1≤i≤r, where each γi is the
meridian around the irreducible component Ci. This basis induces a natural coordinate
system
Char(U) ∼= (C∗)r = {t = (t1, . . . , tr) | ti ∈C∗for any 1 ≤i ≤r}.
For any t ∈Char(U), let Lt denote the corresponding rank one C-local system on U.

Remark 3.3. A similar proof is also used for [BL19, Theorem 1.5] to study the length
of the perverse sheaves Rg∗Lt[2], where g is the open inclusion form U to B. The proof
of Theorem 1.2 indeed shows that the length of the perverse sheaves Rg∗Lt[2] satisﬁes
the formula in [BL19, Theorem 2.4] as equality for any t ∈Char(U), see [BL19, Remark
2.5(a)]. As mentioned in [BL19, section 5, Remark 2.5(d)], once such kind of formula
holds as equality, one can get a formula for the characteristic cycles of the perverse
sheaves g!∗Lt[2]. When ti = tj for any 1 ≤i, j ≤r, this formula is not new, and it
coincides with the one computed in [NT05, Theorem 1.1].
